units.translation: Go out to the deep meadow of Lerna, to the flocks and cattle-stalls of your father
less toward the well-drinking stream of Cenchreae
before you come to Caucasus itself
until you reach the Gorgonean plains
I am at the very end of your wanderings
For when you came to the Molossian plains
you rushed to the great gulf of Rhea
she will come to Argos unwillingly
and they crowned with their hands memorials of themselves for their parents in the house, at the chariot of Adrastus
so that each of them, having obtained by lot, might lead his company to the gates
he goes to the tower of the enemy
I see an eagle fleeing to the hearth
to have been saved to this mainland
go to the house
Ida, to the Hermaean crag
leaping over the plain of Asopus to the crag of Cithaeron, it roused another relay of the fire's escort
for there is need of return to the house for safety
many things indeed touch the liver
having come to a city rejoicing in prosperity
nor to run aground on a rocky shore
there is some hope that he will come home again
as the report was being channeled to the house
Where have you brought me? To what dwelling? CHORUS: To that of the Atreidae
you boldly tread to the altar
to proclaim to the citizens a shout to the house here
having met my father at the swift-passing ferry of sorrows
go to the fated house
to this defense
for appearing well to me
to those to whom I have come
I creep to the many-crowned recess
it is right to bring to the statues of the gods
with sword-drawn hand cutting at the neck
I go away to the house
he leads to these women
soon the leaders of this land might be watchers against us
against everything
snow is falling
against the winds
the sheep already stand for the slaughter of fire
I want to slaughter you at this very altar
I seem to lament in vain, living, at a tomb
to go to show the chambers to the holy light of these escorts
to the rays
and I pray to the last light of the sun
will you not stretch out your leg against the goads?
you fight against the reins
do not kick against the goads
and be with me against the enemy
What do you wish to say in turn to this, stranger?
answer word for word, taking your turn
civil strife and boldness against one another
because she watches my tongue and mouth against these women who have harshly refused
What then is the strong wife of Zeus against this?
the things done against the kinsmen
what enmities and affections are there between one another
How then am I pious toward you?
as it is right to open the mouth to friends
we will deliberate about the rest with the city and the gods
I will not be ashamed to tell you my husband-loving ways
I speak to those who know
so that he may not report these things to the rulers
a stranger spoke to a stranger, having met him
tell your parents that Orestes is dead
crying out to you
I will tell you this great oath of Athena
you say
do I speak?
knowing
toward the servants, hiding a feigned laugh within gloomy eyes
looking at the matter
hearing the word
she raised shield-bearing inhabitants, so that you might be faithful to this duty
